Where it began

Akash Deep was born on 15 December 1996 in Dehri, in Bihar. Cricket was not the obvious path where he grew up. Bihar had no working cricket association at the time, so there was no ladder for a young player to climb, and in Sasaram he was the one boy who cared about the game above his schoolbooks.

He kept going anyway. A close friend helped him find a club in Durgapur, where he played tennis-ball matches, and in 2010 he joined a club in the Bengal first-division league.

The player

He started out as a batsman. As he grew taller his coaches asked him to try fast bowling, and he took to it. He worked with the former Bengal quick Ranadeb Bose and within a year was in the Bengal Under-23 side. His first-class debut for Bengal came on Christmas Day 2019, and he went on to play in the Indian Premier League for Royal Challengers Bangalore and Kolkata Knight Riders.

The Test call came in February 2024, for the last three matches of the home series against England. He heard the news while playing in the Ranji Trophy for Bengal. In his first 10 Tests, all played in 2024 and 2025, he took 28 wickets at 35.79, with a best of 6 for 99.

What made him special

His great day came in England in 2025. Brought in for Jasprit Bumrah in the second Test of the series, he took four wickets in the first innings and six in the second, his first ten-wicket match.

Later in that series he was sent in as nightwatchman to shield his captain, Shubman Gill. Nightwatchmen are meant to survive till the morning and then quietly get out. He had other plans: 66, with 12 boundaries, his first Test fifty and the second-highest score by an Indian nightwatchman. His batting average of 11.64 suggests that innings surprised a few people, possibly including him.

Away from the middle

Before the Test call he had already shown his form for India A against the England Lions, taking eleven wickets in two games. He also came close twice before: he was added to India's squads for the 2022 Asian Games and for a one-day series in South Africa in 2023, though he did not get a game either time.

And finally

He became a fast bowler because he kept growing and his coaches noticed. Few careers have owed quite so much to a growth spurt.
